name: Eljasaph
title: Leader of the tribe of Gad
summary: Eljasaph, son of Deuel (also called Reuel), was the leader of the tribe of Gad during the wilderness wanderings. He was appointed by God to stand with Moses during the census and represented his tribe at the dedication of the tabernacle. He played an important administrative and military role in organizing the people of Israel in the desert.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as Leader of the Tribe of Gad
keyEvents.description: Eljasa, son of Deuel, was chosen by God to lead the tribe of Gad and assist Moses in the census.

keyEvents.title: The Census in the Wilderness
keyEvents.description: Eljasa led the counting of the tribe of Gad, which numbered 45,650 men fit for battle over twenty years old.

keyEvents.title: Gad's Camp South of the Tabernacle
keyEvents.description: Eljasa and the tribe of Gad were assigned their place in the camp on the south side of the tabernacle, under the banner of Reuben.

keyEvents.title: Offering at the Altar
keyEvents.description: On the sixth day, Eljasa, son of Deuel, brought his offering at the dedication of the altar in the tabernacle, including a silver plate, a silver basin, a gold bowl with incense, and several animals for sacrifice.

keyEvents.title: Leader of Gad's Military Division
keyEvents.description: Eljasa led the military division of the tribe of Gad when the Israelites broke camp and marched in orderly formation through the wilderness.
